source_title: Rare White House visit by top US commander puts Trump's Iran strike options in focus
source_excerpt: The top US military commander in the Middle East held a rare in-person briefing with US president Donald Trump on Thursday to discuss the state of the Iran war, including the effectiveness of Washingtonâs naval blockade and military options for a possible resumption of major combat operations, according to reports by The Wall Street Journal and Axios.Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command (CENTCOM), met Trump at the White House alongside defence secretary Pete Hegseth, joint chiefs chairman General Dan Caine and other senior officials. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent and White House envoy Steve Witkoff also attended, Axios reported, citing two US officials.Cooper briefed Trump on whether the naval blockade was achieving its objectives, the operation to guide oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz towards global energy markets, and the economic pressure campaign being conducted by the military in coordination with the Treasury Department, according to Axios. WSJ separately reported that the meeting covered military options for Iran and came as Washington weighs resuming major combat operations.The rare in-person briefing comes as Trump pursues two tracks: trying to revive negotiations with Tehran while preparing for the possibility of renewed strikes after the US midterm elections.
